notes.title: The chip selloff had a permit problem
notes.facts: Stocks initially rallied after the U.S. midterms. On Nov. 5, the Nasdaq Composite closed down 5.5% and the SOXX chip ETF fell 12.15%. AP and Reuters reported that investors were worried Democratic wins could bring more scrutiny and restrictions on data-center construction. Stocks rallied again Friday and were up Monday morning.
notes.read: A chip order looks inevitable right up until someone asks where the power is coming from. The selloff fits a market rethinking how fast the buildout can happen. The rally the day after the vote and the rebound that followed are good reasons to keep the causal claim narrow.
notes.watch: Actual permitting votes, utility agreements and changes to customer delivery schedules. If the projects still get power and break ground on time, the market may have priced in a bigger delay than customers are seeing.

notes.title: Phison sold more. The extra sale paid less.
notes.facts: Phison’s quarterly revenue rose 26.8% from the prior quarter in Taiwan dollars. Gross margin went from 65.3% to 59.7%.
notes.read: A bigger receipt feels great. Then you look at what it cost to fill the order. At Phison, the extra sales earned a thinner gross margin than they did the prior quarter.
notes.watch: My December-quarter check is gross margin at or below 57.8%. A higher result would make me revisit how quickly the more expensive inventory is passing through costs.

sources.label: Phison · Q3 results and earnings presentation

notes.title: Sandisk sold off twice. The second drop had company.
notes.facts: Sandisk fell 13.47% on Oct. 30 after beating the top of its revenue guide by $231M. On Nov. 5 it fell another 22.26% in a broad chip selloff. SOXX was down 8.24% and 12.15% on those respective sessions.
notes.read: Two dates, two questions. At earnings I’m watching whether higher shipment volumes can carry growth as price contributes less. A week later, investors were also reassessing whether data-center projects would get built on schedule. Sandisk lagged its benchmark on both days. The gap alone can’t tell me how much blame to assign to either story.
notes.watch: Watch for customer delivery changes before the December-quarter print. At earnings, my checks are at least $6B in data-center sales and non-GAAP gross margin at or below 85.5%.
